key_insight: Dense arrays of asymmetric flexible leaflets in an oscillatory confined flow can rectify motion into net transport, with an optimal balance between viscous forcing and leaflet elasticity.
engineering_relevance: The results suggest a design rule for microfluidic rectifiers and biomimetic transport systems: maximize leaflet interactions while tuning stiffness to an optimal elastoviscous number.
method: Numerically simulated low-Reynolds-number flow through a channel with multiple flexible asymmetric leaflets.
Used symmetrically oscillating plates to remove background asymmetry and isolate leaflet-induced transport.
Built an analytical steady-limit model and extended it to time-dependent channel oscillations.
evidence_signal: The paper reports that high leaflet density increases collective interactions and net transport, and identifies an optimal elastoviscous number that maximizes the flow.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on a confined, idealized low-Reynolds-number setup, so performance may change in more complex geometries or at higher flow inertia.
paper_title: On the rectification of oscillatory flows by flexible leaflets in a confined geometry
